# #006. Robust L1 + L∞ Linear Fit & Free Variables

<!-- section:scenario -->
You are given noisy sensor observations `(x[i], y[i])` ($i = 0, \dots, n-1$), some of which contain sharp outliers. To balance outlier resistance ($L_1$) against worst-case peak error ($L_\infty$), fit a line $\hat{y}_i = a \, x_i + b$ minimizing:

$$
\min_{a, b \in \mathbb{R}} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} |a \, x_i + b - y_i| + \lambda \max_{0 \le i < n} |a \, x_i + b - y_i|
$$

where $\lambda = \text{linfWeight} \ge 0$. Notice that **both slope $a$ and intercept $b$ are unrestricted real numbers** ($a, b \in (-\infty, +\infty)$)!

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P006Input`)**:
  - `x: number[]`, `y: number[]` — data point coordinates
  - `linfWeight: number` — weight $\lambda$ on the Chebyshev ($L_\infty$) worst residual
- **Output (`P006Output`)**:
  - `slope: number` — fitted slope $a \in \mathbb{R}$
  - `intercept: number` — fitted intercept $b \in \mathbb{R}$
  - `objective: number` — minimized $L_1 + \lambda L_\infty$ error

<!-- section:example -->
For `x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, `y = [3, 5, 7, 9, 25]`, `linfWeight = 2.0`:

- Notice how the first four points lie on $y = 2x + 1$ while `(5, 25)` is an outlier.
- Balancing total $L_1$ against $2 \times L_\infty$ yields **`slope = 4.8`, `intercept = -4.6`**, achieving minimum error **`28.0`**.
- **Important Trap**: `intercept = -4.6` is **negative**! If you leave the solver's default `lb = 0`, `intercept` gets clamped at `0`, yielding an inferior objective (`SUBOPTIMAL`)!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Almost all LP APIs default continuous variables to **non-negative (`lb = 0`)**! Here both `slope` and `intercept` can be negative (Case 2 has `slope ≈ -4.43, intercept = -1.0`), so explicitly pass `lb: -Infinity` in WaSHI or `lb=-highspy.kHighsInf, ub=highspy.kHighsInf` in `highspy`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Linearize $|a x_i + b - y_i|$ using non-negative per-point error variables `e[i] >= 0`:
- `e[i] >= a * x[i] + b - y[i]`
- `e[i] >= -(a * x[i] + b - y[i])`
Then introduce one epigraph variable `mErr >= 0` with `mErr >= e[i]` for every $i$, and minimize `sum(e) + linfWeight * mErr`!

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \, e, m \ge 0} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} e_i + \lambda \, m \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & -e_i \le a x_i + b - y_i \le e_i && \forall i \\
& e_i \le m && \forall i \\
& a, b \in (-\infty, +\infty), \; e_i \ge 0, \; m \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

Always verify whether physical or statistical variables (`slope`, `intercept`, temperature deviations, net flows) are naturally signed or non-negative before trusting solver defaults (`lb = 0`).
